title: Exercises on 後で・後に・後は
description: 10 questions on the differences between 後で, 後に, and 後は: sequence, later events, topic marking, and usage.

questions.prompt: ご飯を食べた後で勉強する。
questions.question: What does 後で mainly highlight in this sentence?
options: A straightforward sequence of actions: first I eat, then I study.
The period after the meal as the new topic of the sentence.
A particularly significant consequence of eating.
The fact that studying must begin immediately after the meal.
questions.explanation: 後で mainly presents the chronological order of two actions: A is completed and B happens afterward. Here, the central idea is simply 'first I eat, then I study,' without turning what follows into the topic or emphasizing a particular consequence.

questions.prompt: 彼は後に有名な作家となった。
questions.question: Which nuance of 後に is especially clear in this sentence?
options: An everyday action postponed until later.
A later point or stage in the narrative.
Something that still remains to be done after completing a task.
A habitual action that occurs every time after a particular event.
questions.explanation: 後に can bring a later moment or stage in the timeline into sharper focus and is common in narrative or descriptive contexts. Here, it means that at a later stage in his life, he became a famous writer.

questions.prompt: 準備はできた。後は出発するだけだ。
questions.question: How should 後は be understood in this context?
options: We will leave at some unspecified time later.
Leaving is an unavoidable consequence of the preparations.
The preparations are finished, and as for the rest, all that remains is to leave.
We will leave immediately after finishing the preparations.
questions.explanation: Here, 後は does not simply indicate that one event happens after another. は brings what remains to be done to the foreground: the preparations are complete, and 'as for the rest,' all that remains is to leave.

questions.prompt: 仕事の後はビールを飲む。
questions.question: What role does は play in 後は?
options: It turns 後 into a numerical duration expression.
It presents the period after work as the topic or context for what follows.
It necessarily indicates that drinking is an immediate consequence of work.
It makes the sentence more formal than 後に.
questions.explanation: In 後は, the particle は topicalizes what comes afterward. 仕事の後は therefore presents 'the period after work' as the context being discussed: as for what I do after work, I drink a beer.

questions.question: Which description best captures the general difference between these two forms?
options: 後で always indicates a long interval, while 後に always indicates a short one.
後で mainly presents the straightforward sequence A → B, while 後に can bring the later moment, event, or stage into sharper focus.
後で belongs exclusively to spoken Japanese, while 後に belongs exclusively to written Japanese.
後で expresses future events, while 後に can only be used for past events.
questions.explanation: Both forms can express posteriority and may overlap in some contexts. The main difference discussed in the article concerns perspective: 後で primarily highlights the sequence of actions, while 後に can give greater prominence to the later moment or event.

questions.prompt: 今は忙しいから、後でやる。
questions.question: Why is 後で especially natural in this sentence?
options: Because 後で is common in everyday Japanese for simply saying that something will be done later.
Because 後で turns what comes afterward into the topic of the conversation.
Because 後で is the most formal way to express temporal succession.
Because 後で always requires the amount of time that will pass to be stated.
questions.explanation: 後で is extremely common in everyday speech with the simple meaning 'later' or 'afterward.' Here, the speaker postpones the action to a later time without adding a particular narrative or topical nuance.

questions.question: Which completion is correct if you want to say 'I'll be back in five minutes'?
options: 後に
後で
後は
の後で
questions.explanation: With numerical durations, Japanese uses patterns such as 五分後に and 三年後に: 'five minutes later / in five minutes' and 'three years later / in three years.' In this use, 後 is read as ご (go), so 五分後に is pronounced ごふんごに. 五分後で is not normally used with this meaning.

questions.prompt: 食べた後で・会議の後に・仕事の後は
questions.question: What do these examples show about how the constructions are formed?
options: 後で, 後に, and 後は can only follow a verb in the ～て form.
A verb normally appears in the ～た form, while a noun is normally followed by の.
後は can follow a noun but not a verb.
後に can only follow numerical time expressions.
questions.explanation: The constructions discussed in the article typically follow a verb in the ～た form, as in 食べた後で, or a noun followed by の, as in 会議の後に and 仕事の後は. 後に can also directly follow duration expressions such as 三年後に.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the contrast presented in the article?
options: Aた後でB expresses simple posteriority between A and B, while AてからB can more clearly emphasize the completion of A as the starting point for B.
Aた後でB indicates that A and B happen simultaneously, while AてからB indicates succession.
AてからB is necessarily more formal than Aた後でB.
The two constructions always have exactly the same meaning and are interchangeable in every context.
questions.explanation: Both constructions may be translated as 'after doing A, do B,' but the article distinguishes the simple posteriority expressed by Aた後でB from the stronger emphasis ～てから can place on the completion of A as the point from which B begins.

questions.prompt: 宿題は全部終わった。＿＿寝るだけだ。
questions.question: Which form best completes the sentence if the speaker means 'The homework is done; now all that's left is to go to bed'?
options: 後で
後に
後は
五分後に
questions.explanation: 後は is especially natural when a previous situation has already been completed and the speaker introduces what remains to be done. 宿題は全部終わった。後は寝るだけだ therefore means 'I've finished all my homework; now all that's left is to go to bed.'
